text: Anthropic opened its directory submission portal, for plugins and MCP connectors, on September 25, 2026.
source_labels: Anthropic, September 25, 2026: Build plugins for Claude with the directory submission portal | Claude docs: Publish to the directory

text: The portal accepts two kinds of submission: an MCP connector, given as a remote server URL and listed in the Connectors Directory, or a plugin bundle hosted on GitHub and listed in the Claude plugin directory.
source_labels: Anthropic, September 25, 2026: Build plugins for Claude with the directory submission portal | Claude docs: Publish to the directory | Claude docs: Submit a connector to the directory | Claude docs: Plugin pre-submission checklist

text: Plugin and connector submissions go through automated checks and a safety scan.
source_labels: Anthropic, September 25, 2026: Build plugins for Claude with the directory submission portal | Claude docs: Publish to the directory

text: Plugin and connector publishers see each submission's review status in the developer portal, and the changes Anthropic asks for.
source_labels: Anthropic, September 25, 2026: Build plugins for Claude with the directory submission portal | Claude docs: Track your directory submission

text: Once a plugin version passes review, you select Publish. By default an Anthropic reviewer then publishes it, and Anthropic can let later versions publish automatically.
source_labels: Claude docs: Submit your plugin | Anthropic, September 25, 2026: Build plugins for Claude with the directory submission portal

text: Plugins and MCP connectors have the same submitter rules: Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise plans can submit; free accounts can't. On Team and Enterprise an Owner submits, and on Enterprise an Owner can also grant the Directory permission to other members.
source_labels: Claude docs: Publish to the directory | Claude docs: Submit a connector to the directory

text: New Connectors Directory listings carry the Community label. Anthropic may escalate a connector to Verified review on its own: there is no application, and Verified reviewers run a functional test of each tool.
source_labels: Claude docs: Connector verification | Claude docs: Connector pre-submission checklist

text: After launch, plugin publishers see installs by product surface and version, listing views, and the searches that lead to a listing.
source_labels: Anthropic, September 25, 2026: Build plugins for Claude with the directory submission portal

text: Claude supports two MCP extensions for connectors and the plugins built on them: MCP Apps, for interactive UI inside chat, and Enterprise Managed Auth, for zero-touch OAuth for enterprise users.
source_labels: Anthropic, September 25, 2026: Build plugins for Claude with the directory submission portal | Claude docs: Submit a connector to the directory

text: Claude connects to a remote MCP server with OAuth 2.0, where each user signs in, with a static API key or bearer token that an organization Owner enters once (in beta, for a limited set of organizations), or with no authentication.
source_labels: Claude docs: Authentication for connectors

text: Every tool has a title and the applicable hint: readOnlyHint for read-only tools, destructiveHint for tools that modify or delete data.
source_labels: Claude docs: Connector pre-submission checklist

text: Tool names are 64 characters or fewer.
source_labels: Claude docs: Connector pre-submission checklist

text: Tool descriptions say what the tool does and when to use it. They must not tell Claude how to behave.
source_labels: Claude docs: Connector pre-submission checklist

text: A single tool that mixes safe and unsafe HTTP methods, such as a catch-all api_request tool, is rejected. Read and write actions go in separate tools.
source_labels: Claude docs: Connector pre-submission checklist

text: A connector submission includes test credentials for a fully populated account.
source_labels: Claude docs: Connector pre-submission checklist

text: For a plugin bundle, the first organization to submit a repository folder holds that listing.
source_labels: Claude docs: Publish to the directory

text: A domain verification token is served at /.well-known/openai-apps-challenge on the MCP server's host or a parent host.
source_labels: OpenAI Developers: Submit plugins

text: The submitter has a verified individual or business identity.
source_labels: OpenAI Developers: Submit plugins

text: The submitter has Apps Management write access.
source_labels: OpenAI Developers: Submit plugins

text: The submission includes exactly five positive and three negative test cases.
source_labels: OpenAI Developers: Plugin submission errors | OpenAI Developers: Submit plugins

text: The submission includes a demo recording.
source_labels: OpenAI Developers: Plugin submission errors

text: The submission includes release notes that summarize the version being submitted and what changed.
source_labels: OpenAI Developers: Submit plugins | OpenAI Developers: Plugin submission errors

text: The submission lists website, support, privacy policy and terms of service URLs.
source_labels: OpenAI Developers: Submit plugins

text: Reviewer test credentials work without MFA, SMS or email confirmation, or private-network access.
source_labels: OpenAI Developers: Submit plugins

text: Every MCP tool sets readOnlyHint, openWorldHint and destructiveHint to match what it does, with a justification for each.
source_labels: OpenAI Developers: Plugin submission errors | OpenAI Developers: Remote MCP server review requirements

text: To restrict access by workspace domain, the OAuth server has a UserInfo endpoint that returns email_verified, and it offers the openid and email scopes.
source_labels: OpenAI Developers: Authentication

text: Projects with EU data residency cannot currently submit MCP plugins.
source_labels: OpenAI Developers: Remote MCP server review requirements

text: Published plugins appear in the Plugins Directory shared by ChatGPT and Codex.
source_labels: OpenAI Developers: Submit plugins | OpenAI Developers: Remote MCP server review requirements

text: After publication, OpenAI periodically fetches your MCP tools. Deleted tools are removed as soon as a scan finds them, and changed tools go live once they pass automated checks.
source_labels: OpenAI Developers: Submit plugins | OpenAI Developers: Remote MCP server review requirements

text: Plugins are submitted at cursor.com/marketplace/publish from a public Git repository. Every plugin is manually reviewed before it is listed.
source_labels: Cursor Docs: Plugins reference | Cursor Docs: Plugins

text: Cursor accepts a root plugin.json (the Agent Plugins standard) or a .cursor-plugin/plugin.json (a Cursor Plugin). Plugin names are lowercase kebab-case.
source_labels: Cursor Docs: Plugins | Cursor Docs: Plugins reference

text: Open-source components must use permissive licenses, such as MIT, BSD or Apache 2.0. GPL, AGPL and LGPL are not allowed.
source_labels: Cursor Marketplace Publisher Terms

text: Team marketplaces are available on the Teams plan (one marketplace) and the Enterprise plan (unlimited).
source_labels: Cursor Docs: Plugins

text: A remote server is published with a server.json whose remotes property lists its URL, and the server must be publicly accessible there.
source_labels: MCP Registry: Publishing remote servers

text: You authenticate the namespace you publish under: GitHub for io.github.* names, or DNS or HTTP for a domain you control.
source_labels: MCP Registry: How to authenticate when publishing

text: The registry is in preview: breaking changes or data resets may happen before general availability.
source_labels: MCP Registry: Publishing remote servers | MCP Registry: How to authenticate when publishing

text: MCP 2026-07-28 removed sessions and the initialize handshake, made servers implement server/discover, and deprecated Dynamic Client Registration in favor of Client ID Metadata Documents. DCR still works for backward compatibility, for now. Servers built last year need work.
source_labels: MCP blog, July 28, 2026: The 2026-07-28 specification | MCP specification 2026-07-28: Key changes
